title: Investigate FP8 prefill regression on long-context prompts (H100/H200)
creator: Noah Patel
body:
## Summary
We’re seeing a repeatable performance regression in FP8 **prefill** on long-context prompts (8k–32k tokens) relative to FP16 baseline and/or prior runtime builds. Decode performance looks within expected variance; the regression primarily manifests as elevated prefill latency and degraded tokens/sec during the initial prompt ingestion phase.

This issue blocks recommending FP8 defaults for long-context workloads in the sprint report and affects Dedicated prospects evaluating long-context chat.

## Environment / where it shows up
- GPUs: H100 SXM (primary), H200 (secondary confirmation)
- Runtime: perf-lab builds around runtime-1.20 branch cut (see build stamps in benchmark artifacts)
- Quant mode: FP8 enabled (e4m3/e5m2 per current policy)
- Workload shape: long-context prompt sets (prefill-heavy), moderate concurrency (2–8), non-streaming and streaming show similar prefill behavior

## Repro steps (benchmark-lab)
1) Use the long-context preset ("lc_*" prompt distribution) for Llama/Qwen families.
2) Run with pinned clocks + pinned container digest (per ENG-24812).
3) Compare FP16 vs FP8 prefill phase metrics:
   - prefill_ms (or phase-prefill) p50/p95
   - prefill tokens/sec
   - GPU kernel timeline for attention/GEMM

Notes:
- The regression is most pronounced at 16k+ context and at certain head_dim alignment boundaries.

## Initial hypotheses
H1) **Alignment/stride handling bug** causing inefficient memory access or fallback kernel selection for certain sequence lengths.
H2) Kernel auto-selector picking a suboptimal FP8 attention kernel configuration for long-context (tile/launch config mismatch).
H3) Unintended extra casts/scale conversions inside prefill path for FP8 when context is large (KV/cache interaction overhead).

## Profiling notes / findings
### Key observation
Nsight Systems traces show longer-than-expected FP8 attention kernels during prefill at long sequence lengths, with evidence of non-ideal memory transactions and lower SM occupancy than expected. The slowdown correlates with specific shapes.

### What we checked
- Verified GPU clocks pinned and no major contention (perf-lab node isolation looked OK for the failing runs).
- Confirmed regression persists across multiple repetitions (not a one-off outlier).
- With additional tracing enabled (see PR redwood/pr_10621), kernel family and shape logging indicated the FP8 prefill path is taking a code path that differs from the common-case shapes.

### Root cause (confirmed)
Incorrect alignment handling in the FP8 prefill path for long-context prompts. For certain sequence length / stride combinations, we were effectively mis-handling alignment assumptions and triggering a slower execution path.

## Proposed fix
Implement correct alignment handling for FP8 prefill on long-context prompts and add a targeted regression test for long-context shapes.

- Code change: adjust alignment/stride validation and fast-path eligibility checks for FP8 prefill; ensure correct addressing and avoid slow fallback path.
- Add regression coverage:
  - micro-level: targeted attention kernel test on representative long-context shapes
  - end-to-end: benchmark-lab long-context preset with FP8 enabled; assert prefill phase does not regress beyond thresholds

Implementation tracked/landed in: GitHub redwood/pr_10630

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Repro case no longer shows FP8 prefill regression on H100
- [x] Confirmed on H200 when capacity available
- [x] Add regression test covering 16k/32k shape(s)
- [x] Benchmark-lab run shows prefill p95 within expected band (no >5% regression vs baseline build)
- [x] Note in sprint report + include in release notes highlights

## Follow-ups
- Audit remaining long-context FP8 code paths for similar alignment assumptions (especially around KV/cache interaction).
- Add an alert in perf-canary for long-context prefill (separate from decode).

comments: 2025-10-02 — Noah Patel: Flagging as P0. In the baseline matrix we’re seeing FP8 prefill p95 +12–18% at 16k/32k on H100 vs last week’s pinned commit. Please prioritize root cause; this is the main blocker for FP8 default guidance on long-context.

2025-10-03 — Grace Kim: Able to repro consistently with lc_16k preset on H100. Decode looks normal; prefill phase only. Starting with kernel timeline + verify kernel selection/shape logging once ENG-24814 lands.

2025-10-04 — Isabella Rossi: Ran Nsight Systems on failing shape. FP8 attention kernel duration spikes at specific seq lengths; occupancy drops. Looks like we’re hitting a different path when seq_len not aligned to expected tile. Suspect alignment/stride condition.

2025-10-06 — Grace Kim: Added temporary tracing spans locally (based on redwood/pr_10621 branch) — confirms unusual shape triggers different fast-path eligibility. Working on minimal repro unit test for the alignment guard.

2025-10-07 — Grace Kim: Root cause looks like incorrect alignment handling in FP8 prefill path for long context; can reproduce on small harness by forcing seq_len=16384 with specific head_dim stride. Draft fix prepared, adding targeted regression test.

2025-10-08 — Connor O'Brien: If fix is low-risk + has test coverage, we can take it in runtime-1.20. Please ensure perf-canary scenario isn’t flaky and add a release note line for "FP8 long-context prefill".

2025-10-09 — Grace Kim: Opened PR redwood/pr_10630. Includes fix + regression test. Ran benchmark-lab quick pass on H100: prefill p95 back in line with baseline (within ~1–2%). Waiting on H200 node for confirmation.
2025-10-10 — Grace Kim: H200 confirmation run completed (limited matrix): regression resolved; prefill p95 improved vs failing build. Marking ready once PR merges.
2025-10-11 — Grace Kim: PR merged. Updating sprint report notes and tagging for runtime-1.20 release highlights.
